newsitem.title: USA: Allstate sees risk and reward in Ill. agency deal.
newsitem.headline: Allstate sees risk and reward in Ill. agency deal.

text.p: Allstate Corp's Allstate Insurance Co expects both risk and reward from its Development Finance Authority for social services organizations, a company official said.

Charles Mires, an assistant vice president and manager of the Northbrook, Ill.-based company's municipal bond division, said the company was still reviewing the program and had not made a committment as yet.
He said if the company ultimately decided to buy bonds, it expects a market rate of return, in addition to added risk given that social services agencies would be the borrowers.
On Wednesday, the authority's board generally approved the concept for the program, but withheld final approval of two bond issues until its December meeting.

Bobby Wilkerson, the authority's director, said the bond issues involve a group of African-American social service agencies on Chicago's southside that have a $15 million capital improvement need, and a mental health clinic in Decatur with an approximately $4 million need. The agencies are largely dependent on state of Illinois contracts for their funding, according to Wilkerson.

In place of a letter of credit or bond insurance, the unrated bonds would be sold to Allstate soley with credit enhancement provided by the authority through funds appropriated for that purpose by the Illinois General Assembly.
Mires said the credit and structuring role played by the authority were key to Allstate's interest in the program, which he added would be unique for the company.
"Without the participation of IDFA, it's highly unlikely they could pull off this kind of transaction with us," he added.
Mires said Allstate was attracted to the program due to the social responsiblity aspect of helping out social service agencies within the company's home state.
He added that while Allstate does not have "an unlimited appetite" for deals of this kind, it would be willing to consider similar deals in the future.
